newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss S/A M0 rose 519 mln Sfr y/y in Jan - SNB.
newsitem.headline: Swiss S/A M0 rose 519 mln Sfr y/y in Jan - SNB.

text.p: Switzerland's January seasonally adjusted central bank money supply (M0) rose 519 million Swiss francs ($356.3 million) compared with January 1996 to stand at 32.350 billion francs, the Swiss National Bank (SNB) said.
Commercial banks' sight deposits at the SNB dipped 128 million francs on average to 3.289 billion, while notes in circulation rose 4.7 percent to 29.870 billion.
An SNB spokesman said money supply in January was up an annualised 5.9 percent from the year-earlier month and 11.4 percent compared with the fourth quarter of 1996.
"But this is always somewhat distorted because it is annualised and so the numbers are always a bit high early on (in the year)," he said.
He said the growth reflected the SNB's generous money supply policy.
The SNB said in January it expected seasonally adjusted central bank money supply to rise 0.1 percent in the first quarter of 1997 from the fourth quarter of 1996.
The SNB has said on several occasions it will keep its monetary policy generous until it detects clear signs of an economic upturn after six years of stagnation.
But SNB officials have also made clear in public comments that they do not want to let inflationary pressure grow too strong by keeping policy loose for too long.
